title: La mesa
goal: Order a table and describe the size with your hands
culture: He will build it from what he has and he will not write anything down. Hands are an accepted unit of measurement here and sin prisa is a real instruction — say it and mean it, because saying it and then chasing him is worse than not saying it.

beats.en: I want a table. Could you make me one?
ok: quiero una mesa me la hace
beats.good: ¿Me la hace? asks him to make you one. There is no catalogue and no price list, and that is not a problem to be solved.
Hands are a unit here and he would rather have them than a number. Así de grande with your arms out is a specification.

beats.es: ¿Y de qué material? Tengo pino y tengo cedro.
beats.good: Cedro is the good one and he asked because it costs more. Saying which is how you avoid finding out in a fortnight.

beats.es: Va pues. Démela en quince días, ¿le corre prisa?
beats.good: Sin prisa is a real instruction and he will take it at face value. Say it and then chase him and you have taught him you did not mean it.
